prompt: A media query stacks the columns when the screen is narrower than 600px.
tells: A media query stacks the columns
why: Changing layout by screen size is responsive design.
trap: Flex does the stacking, but the media query is the clue.

prompt: Without the viewport meta tag, the page looks tiny and zoomed out on phones.
tells: looks tiny and zoomed out on phones
why: The viewport tag tells phones to use the device width. That's responsive design.
trap: It's an HTML tag, but its job is fitting the screen.

prompt: On a phone, the page scrolls sideways because a table is wider than the screen.
tells: scrolls sideways because a table is wider than the screen
why: Content that doesn't adapt to narrow screens breaks responsive design.
trap: The box is too wide, but the clue is the phone screen.

prompt: On small screens the menu becomes a single 'Menu' button.
tells: On small screens the menu becomes
why: Changing what's shown by screen size is responsive design.
trap: A click opens it, but the clue is the screen size.

prompt: Images use max-width: 100% so they shrink to fit any screen.
why: Fluid sizes that adapt to the screen are responsive design.
trap: It's sizing, but the purpose is fitting screens.

prompt: The team writes the phone layout first, then adds rules for wider screens.
why: Starting narrow and adding breakpoints is mobile-first responsive design.
trap: The cascade orders it, but the clue is screen widths.
